text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: These findings of ambiguous genitalia, bone fragility, and maternal virilization strongly suggest a disorder of sex development, likely Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone_level, REQUEST TEST: Karyotype

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal 17-hydroxyprogesterone and karyotype results rule out classic CAH and Turner syndrome, so I need to investigate the bone fragility further. REQUEST TEST: Bone_density_scan, REQUEST TEST: Serum_collagen_type_I

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bone density scan: Reduced bone mineral density (osteopenia). Serum collagen type I: Abnormal structure/function.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abnormal collagen type I confirms a defect in bone matrix formation, pointing towards Osteogenesis Imperfecta rather than an endocrine disorder. I will request medical images to assess the extent of skeletal involvement and check for other associated features. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of maternal virilization, ambiguous genitalia, and severe acne strongly suggests 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency, a form of Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia. REQUEST TEST: Plasma_androstenedione_level, REQUEST TEST: Plasma_11-deoxycorticosterone_level
